title: Applied ML evals: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates our Applied ML evaluation standards for model onboarding, prompt set curation and benchmarking, quantization profile selection, automated quality guardrails, and a step-by-step regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and production owners using the eval-harness-service, model-catalog, and the centralized prompt repository.

Scope:
- Onboarding new candidate models into model-catalog for Redwood-hosted serving and Dedicated/private deployments.
- Building and curating prompt sets and benchmarks for task families (dialogue, summarization, classification, code generation, retrieval-augmented generation).
- Defining quantization profiles and recommended accuracy/perf tradeoffs.
- Automated quality guardrails integrated into CI and runtime monitoring.
- Regression triage and escalation process for evaluation and production regressions.

Owners and roles:
- Applied ML (primary): model onboarding, candidate evaluation, prompt curation (Owners: Daniel Kim, Sofia Martinez).
- Serving Runtime (secondary): performance profiling, latency/throughput validation (Owners: Runtime team).
- Product/Platform: requirements, rollout authority, SLAs.
- SRE/Observability: alerting, dashboards, incident response.

Key services and artifacts referenced:
- eval-harness-service: centralized runner for batch + streaming evals; exposes job API and Prometheus metrics.
- model-catalog: registry with model metadata, quantization variants, and verified perf profiles.
- prompt-repo: canonical prompt sets and metadata (task, language, difficulty, expected outputs).
- quality-guardrails: CI checks & runtime hooks (unit tests, threshold gates, log sampling).

Onboarding checklist (required for a candidate model):
1) Pre-screening: compatibility with serving runtime (supported ops/kernels). Command: `ci-checks --model <id> --compatibility`
2) Baseline eval: run eval-harness job for canonical prompt sets (low/medium/high difficulty).
   - Required metrics: Rouge-L, ROUGE-1, F1, Exact Match (task-dependent), Perplexity, and calibrated confidence scores for classification.
   - Latency: p50 and p95 token-generation measured on representative sequence lengths (see performance section).
3) Quantization sweep: run standard 8-bit and 4-bit quantization profiles (see Quantization Profiles table below).
4) Repro and determinism: run 10 exemplar inference runs and verify top-k output stability where applicable.
5) Security/compliance checklist: ensure no disallowed external calls, licensing checks, and embed model license into model-catalog entry.
6) Sign-off: applied-ml reviewer + runtime reviewer + product owner.

Prompt sets and benchmark guidelines:
- Prompt metadata: every prompt must include task, input schema, expected output format, difficulty (easy/medium/hard), domain tags, and golden reference(s) when available.
- Sampling: prompt sets should include at least 500 examples for broad benchmarks, and a minimum of 50 for targeted checks or fast pre-screening.
- Split: provide train/validation/test partitions for regression tracking where human labels exist.
- Metrics: choose task-appropriate metrics; for multi-turn dialogue prefer human-eval proxies (consistency, helpfulness) plus automated metrics such as BLEU/ROUGE and embedding-based similarity (cosine on model-embedding).
- Bias and safety checks: include adversarial and safety prompt subset (minimum 25 prompts) that exercises content policy boundaries and known failure modes.
- Versioning: each prompt-set file should include a semantic version (v1.0.0), changelog, and owner.

Benchmarking: standard tasks and thresholds (examples)
- Summarization (news domain): ROUGE-L >= 0.35 baseline; degrade >5% from production baseline triggers triage.
- Classification (intent): Macro-F1 >= 0.82; delta >= 0.03 triggers regression alert.
- Code generation (Python snippets): pass-rate on unit tests >= 0.60; regression if delta >= 0.10.
- Latency SLOs for hosted API (p95 generation latency): <= 450 ms for short prompt (<=128 tokens) on default instance types; p50 <= 120 ms.
- Embeddings (semantic search): cosine similarity to reference embeddings >= 0.88 on held-out set.

Quality guardrails (automated + human-in-the-loop):
- CI gates (pre-merge): all eval-harness jobs for changed models or prompt-sets must pass with defined thresholds. CI job names: `eval-harness/baseline`, `eval-harness/quant-sweep`, `eval-harness/safety-checks`.
- Pre-rollout checks: smoke test on canary traffic (1% of production), monitoring for latency, error rate, and evaluation metrics over the canary prompts.
- Runtime guardrails: automatic fallback policy in model-catalog for throughput/latency breaches (route to a higher-latency but more-robust variant), token-level anomaly detection for hallucination spikes, safety classifier hook for policy violations.
- Human review: when automated checks fail or show borderline regressions, trigger a human review with the applied-ml reviewer group using the `eval-triage` channel and linked ticket in the triage board.

Quantization profiles (recommended defaults)
- Profile candidates are stored as tags in model-catalog (`q8_default`, `q4_mixed`, `q4_static`, `q2_experimental`).
- Example profile table (plain-text):

| profile_name   | bit-width | expected_quality_delta | recommended_use_case                  | owner | notes |
|----------------|-----------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------|-------|
| q8_default     | 8         | ~0.5% drop             | general-purpose low-regret deployments | Quant team | safe default, fastest compile path |
| q4_mixed       | 4         | ~1.5-3% drop           | cost-sensitive inference with caching  | Quant team | mixed-precision for attention layers |
| q4_static      | 4         | ~2-4% drop             | latency-critical with aggressive cost  | Quant team | test on long sequences before deploy |
| q2_experimental| 2         | >=4% drop              | research / ultra-cost experiments      | Research | requires manual review & sign-off |

- Quant sweep process: run `eval-harness --job quant-sweep --profiles q8_default,q4_mixed,q4_static` and generate a report with quality vs latency/cost curves. Save report artifact in S3 at `s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/<model-id>/<run-id>/`. Attach artifact to model-catalog entry.

Regression triage playbook (incident-style for eval regressions):
1) Alerting: regression alerts are generated by the eval-monitor job or runtime guardrails and posted to Slack channel `#eval-regressions` and to the triage board. Alert payload includes metric, delta, affected prompt subset, and recent deploy IDs.
2) Initial triage (within 1 hour): assigned applied-ml engineer runs: reproduce locally with `eval-harness --job reproduce --run-id <alert-run-id>`, check model-catalog variant, compare to last-good artifact, and collect logs + golden prompt examples.
3) Classification: determine scope — scoped (single prompt subset), broad (many tasks/domains), or infra (latency/throughput regression).
4) Priority and escalations:
   - P0 (user-facing production regression affecting >10% of traffic or >5% absolute metric drop): page oncall SRE and product owner; roll back to last-good model variant and open Sev ticket.
   - P1 (significant but contained regression): notify applied-ml and runtime, create remediation branch and schedule hotfix.
   - P2 (minor or non-user-facing): create backlog item and schedule for next iteration.
5) Mitigation steps:
   - If quality regression coincides with quantization change: redeploy previous quant profile (e.g., q8_default).
   - If regression coincides with prompt-set change: revert prompt-set commit and re-run eval-harness.
   - If regression coincides with runtime/kernel changes: notify serving runtime team and run targeted perf/accuracy tests on affected kernels.
6) Postmortem: for P0/P1 events produce a 72-hour postmortem with root cause analysis, timeline, mitigation, and preventative actions. Attach to related_pages and link to the authorized model-catalog entry.

Operational runbooks and commands (common):
- Run a baseline eval: `eval-harness run --model <model-id> --prompts canonical/summarization --metrics rouge,perplexity --out report.json`
- Compare two runs: `eval-harness compare --base <run-id> --candidate <run-id> --report diffs.md`
- Trigger quant sweep: `eval-harness quant-sweep --model <model-id> --profiles q8_default,q4_mixed`
- Promote a model variant: update model-catalog metadata and use `catalog promote --model <id> --variant <variant> --traffic 0.1` for canary rollout.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Dashboards: `applied-ml/model-health` (quality deltas, regression history), `applied-ml/latency-cost` (p50/p95, cost-per-token by variant), `applied-ml/safety` (policy hits over time).
- Alerts: configured in Prometheus/Alertmanager; key alert thresholds are set in the model-catalog metadata for each model (fields: `alert_thresholds.metric_name`, `alert_thresholds.delta`).

Documentation and training:
- All teams must follow this playbook for onboarding and regression processes.
- Quarterly training sessions will be run by Applied ML to walk through the eval-harness, quantization tradeoffs, and triage practice using historical incidents.

References and related pages:
- Applied ML Eval Harness standards: /applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Prompt sets guidelines: /applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026
- Quantization profiles central registry: model-catalog -> quantization section

Appendix: example eval-harness job manifest (YAML snippet)

```yaml
job_name: summarization_baseline
model_id: redwood/small-summarizer-v2
prompts: canonical/summarization/v1
metrics: [rouge-l,rouge-1,perplexity]
profiles: [q8_default]
artifact_s3: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/redwood-small-summarizer-v2/2027-01-10/
```
